text: Okay then, I will do that. One second. There we go. Good morning, fellow workers of the court, judges Zayas, Winkler and Bach of the appeals court and Mr. Winters and Gentry counsel for the plaintiff. I would like to reserve two minutes of my time for response to plaintiff's oral arguments. This tale of disillusionment, which is a good thing, is primarily for my daughters. I intend to speak to everyone as my equal. I especially want those without law degrees to understand my remarks. As is customary for technical writers like me, I will define special terms, especially my idiosyncratic noun phrases, before I use them. I won't define terms like idiosyncratic, which you can look up in Wikipedia. A mortal of misfortune is a flesh and blood human being that has had the misfortune to lose a job, have an accident or get a disease that led to an inability to pay a debt through no fault of their own. I am a mortal of misfortune because I lost my job by layoff, not for cause and was unable to find another. Every mortal of misfortune has a story that deserves respect and consideration. Corporations like Crown Asset Management LLC and Levy & Associates LLC are artificial persons before the law. They are artificial persons that were created in perpetuity to accumulate wealth and they have owners. Euphemisms aside, any person, artificial or natural, who has an owner is a slave. An owner of a slave is a slave owner because these immortal corporations were created only to accumulate wealth through profit. I call them immortal slaves of fortune. That is what they are. I call their owners slave owners because that is what they are. The state courts in Ohio, including this appeals court, are also immortals. They were here long before the judges in court today were born and will be here long after they have passed. The courts are a special kind of immortal because they purport to represent the citizens in their quest for truth and justice. In fact, the judges in court today are elected officials. Consequently, I call the courts immortal representatives of truth and justice for the people. We are here today because I strenuously objected to the trial court judge granting a continuance at plaintiff's request just when I was prepared to appear in court to make the case that I have now made in my final brief. I objected to the continuance because I knew that I was moving out of Ohio to avoid homelessness in Cincinnati. When mortals move, their lives are disrupted. I knew I would not be able to represent myself adequately during that time and so did the lawyers for the plaintiff. Despite acknowledging my objection, the trial court granted the continuance and I was effectively prevented from pressing my requests for discovery in a timely manner or presenting my arguments in court by the summary judgment that quickly followed. All I was able to muster was my ill-titled affidavit for trial. Let me be clear, at the trial court level, I did not want to go to court. I explicitly requested an out-of-court settlement in pretrial negotiations and I did not want to represent myself. However, once I realized that no lawyer would represent me at a reasonable cost and that my income was exempt from garnishment because I live only on my social security, I resigned myself to my pro se defense at trial and I turned my attention to the redacted complaint itself. As an amateur logician, I quickly realized that as a consequence of the redactions and omissions, the complaint neither proved ownership of the debt obligation at issue in the case nor that I had digitally signed the redacted promissory note included there. There were no notarized affidavits of the signatories of the debt obligation sale and the integrity of the document was destroyed by the redactions. Additionally, there was no digital artifact for a signature that included cryptographical non-repudiation. After answering plaintiff's discovery requests in a timely fashion, I drafted my own discovery requests and submitted them. However, plaintiff's savvy lawyers were neither timely nor responsive to my requests as their professional code of conduct requires. Instead, they took advantage of my inexperience and delayed, denied relevance and ignored my legitimate discovery requests. Since I did not realize that when confronted with such tactics, I should have asked the court for enforcement, I missed my opportunity to get responsive answers to my legitimate discovery requests. Unless this court remains the case to their trial court level, it appears that the cheating in that way by plaintiff's law firm will be rewarded. And so I came to understand that plaintiff believes that it has a right to what I call a veil of inscrutability. A veil of this kind is like a curtain behind which plaintiff could hide embarrassing information like what they paid for the debt obligation or the profit rates they enjoy. For example, they ignored my pretrial request for the price they paid for the debt obligation at issue in this case. They redacted the complaint improperly by hiding information that was not personal. In so doing, plaintiff and its law firm destroyed the integrity of the document and prevented any detection and analysis of its possible manipulation as I showed in my final brief, Appendix C. The plaintiff and its law firm did all of this with impunity because they know that the courts will protect their veil of inscrutability. As a first-time pro se defendant, I was under the illusion that I might be able to pierce the plaintiff's veil of inscrutability by appealing the summary judgment. After the appeal was approved, I reached out to Mr. Walsh, who was the plaintiff's attorney at the time, and asked him to give me a summary judgment of the plaintiff's complaint. The plaintiff's attorney, Mr. Walsh, gave me a summary judgment of the plaintiff's complaint. After the appeal was approved, I reached out to Mr. Winters via email to attempt to get him to correct his firm's egregiously unruly behavior with respect to my discovery requests. He graciously informed me that no discovery is permitted at the appeals level. Basically, he said, snooze, you lose, we got away with it. And so I was disillusioned in that respect. And that was not my last disillusionment. I was still under the illusion that if I were to make an appeal, that the constitutional issue would be addressed as a priority, overriding local rules. After all, I thought the constitution is the law of the land, par excellence. Working under that illusion, I began mining data from the clerk of court's website. I downloaded all the data for all the cases handled by Levy & Associates in 2019, the last year before the pandemic. I created a database, developed graphics, prepared tables, and wrote a narrative that tied together, excuse me, all of my research. As an amateur logician, I prepared an appendix that used the propositional calculus to prove the validity of a formal analogy. And I based my legal argument on those solid foundations. That motion used the data from the clerk of court's own website to show that Levy & Associates, their clients, and the Hamilton County Courts together, formed a system of wealth extraction. That system takes the wealth of defenseless Hamilton County mortals of misfortune out of the county and out of the state, distributing it across the country as profits to the slave owners of the debt buyer clients of Levy & Associates, like Crown Asset Management. That system, I showed, extracted more than $3 million from the county that year, and it did so in a biased fashion. I showed that the over extraction of wealth from some zip codes corresponded to those in which Black and African Americans were overrepresented. How coincidental. And the magnitude was not inconsequential. Some such zip codes had almost four times as much wealth extracted for them as one would expect from their population, hardly equal protection under the law. So that motion showed that the clients of Levy & Associates are a special kind of immortal slave of fortune. They are socioeconomic vampires. They are like Alex and his droogs in a clockwork orange when they find that tramp, a mortal of misfortune indeed, under a highway overpass, and begin to literally kick him while he is down. Like that clockwork orange mortal of misfortune, I and the hundreds of other mortals of misfortune set upon by these socioeconomic vampires are defenseless because there is no mandate for public defenders in civil court cases in the home of the brave and the land of the free. Surely such behavior is untenable, I thought. However, the court disillusioned me again by ruling that my motion was, quote, not well taken, unquote. I had no idea what that meant. So I decided to ask the court what it meant. When I filed a request for the court to explain its ruling, it responded that my request too was, quote, not well taken, unquote. I concluded that in order to protect the veil of inscrutability of the plaintiffs, the court had wrapped itself in a similar veil. Perhaps despite being elected by the people, the justices on the court were not the immortal representatives of truth and justice for the people that I had imagined them to be. Undaunted, I reminded myself that my true goal was to show simply that the plaintiff and its law firm by relying exclusively on the improperly redacted complaint had not met the burden of proof they assumed when bringing the complaint to the trial court. That is what I demonstrated, excuse me, very effectively in my final brief. I realize now, however, that I was under the illusion while I was writing that final brief that this appeals court could provide the relief that I asked for there. I expect to be disillusioned again in that respect. I have spent almost two years of my life struggling to be disillusioned enough to get the help of the courts to pierce the veil of inscrutability that the plaintiffs presume I have a right to enjoy, they have a right to enjoy. During that time, I have struggled to find shelter and the simple accommodations necessary to write the motions and briefs I've presented. Last fall, after trying for almost three years, I was finally granted a job interview. I aced the interview and was offered the job. However, by that time I was homeless, living in my tiny car and at a nearby campground. I had to turn down the job because the salary was insufficient to permit me to get an apartment. I was able to complete my final brief only because of the solidarity of a good Samaritan who allowed me to sleep and work out of one room of her house. I know that life is not always fair and it is not the job of the courts to ensure fairness. I also know that laws can sometimes be passed that make life for defenseless mortals of misfortune like me and the hundreds of us every year in Hamilton County that are affected by the operation of the immortal vampire slaves of fortune like Crown Asset Management and its debt collector law firm a bit fairer. Finally, I realize, and I hope the court does too, that such beneficial laws only happen when the intolerable abuses are not protected by a veil of inscrutability. Legislators need to know of the abuses to write enlightened legislation and the public needs to know of them to hold the legislators accountable. If the courts are the immortal representatives of truth and justice for the people that I imagine they could be, then they have a role in the democratic betterment of the fate of defenseless mortals of misfortune like me. In the contest between these immortal vampire slaves of fortune and the defenseless mortals of misfortune that seek only to shine the daylight of public scrutiny on the profits of the vampires, whose side are the courts on? Please find a way to strip away the veil of inscrutability that protects the immortal vampire slaves of fortune so that the people and their legislative representatives can act in an informed and humane way. Send this case back to the trial court with the admonition to conduct the discovery and scrutiny of the complaint in accordance with the law and the appropriate placement of the burden of proof if you are not able to do that in this appeals court. Ask also please for plaintiff's law firm to respect the rules of professional conduct that presumably apply to that firm. I will do my part by filing a complaint with the appropriate bar associations for the egregiously unruly behavior of the firm to date. Thank you.
